sources.entry: Chyrp Lite - Extra-awesome, extra-lightweight blog engine. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause PHP

summary.one_liner: Chyrp Lite is a lightweight, self-hostable PHP blog engine with support for multiple post types (Feathers), standalone Pages, and optional modules.
summary.what_it_does: Chyrp Lite lets you host a blog on your own web server, supporting a traditional blog, a tumblelog, or a general-purpose publishing site with blogging features. Its Feathers system provides post types for text, photo, quote, link, video, audio, and multi-file uploads, and text can be written as plain text, Markdown, or raw markup. Pages publish standalone articles, including hierarchies and an optional homepage. A set of modules adds features such as comments, tags, categories, webmentions, likes, a sitemap, a math-problem anti-spam check, syntax highlighting, caching, and a Content Security Policy header. Themes are built with the Twig template engine, and the admin console includes a rights model for users and visitors.
use_cases: run a tumblelog with multiple post types
publish standalone pages like a colophon or site hierarchy
accept comments and webmentions on a blog
build a custom blog theme with Twig
host photo, video, or audio posts on my own server
how_to_run: If using MySQL, create a MySQL database with a username and password.
Download the latest release, unzip, and upload to your web server.
Run the installation process by visiting install.php in your web browser.
Docker: download the latest release and unzip it.
Docker: read through docker-compose.yaml and modify if needed.
Docker: run `docker compose up -d --build` to build and start the container, then visit install.php.
notable: Feathers system for distinct post types such as text, photo, quote, link, video, and audio
Modular extension system with more than 20 optional modules
Responsive, W3C-validated HTML5 with ARIA labelling
Supports plain text, Markdown, or raw markup in posts
caveats: Posts and pages may contain arbitrary HTML, JavaScript, and CSS, so untrusted authors need the Content Security Policy module enabled
Several README and license files are publicly accessible after installation and may need access restrictions
Requires a PHP host with specific extensions and a supported database (MySQL, SQLite, or PostgreSQL)
keywords: run a blog on my own server
